title: Streams
how_read: Today's streams; they follow the draws of the 1975 photo map and the blue lines of 1959.

title: Rivers, as Mouzon draws them (1775), fitted to today's courses
how_read: Picked by hand every 50-100 pixels of a half-resolution crop and snapped by program to the engraved line; fitted to the ground by matching them to today's rivers (Natural Earth). Rivers with no line in Natural Earth (Pacolet, Tyger, Enoree, Black, Ashley, Combahee), and since the refit of 26 Nov 2026 the Pee Dee, Little Pee Dee and Waccamaw, follow the fit and are low. Each river is one line, joined across the strips where the scan's mounted sections meet (2-6 km).

title: The sea coast, as Mouzon draws it, and the sea
how_read: The outer coast snapped to the engraved line and fitted to today's coast. Inlets, islands and the sounds behind them are not traced yet: the sea is closed across the harbour mouths.

title: The main roads of 1775, as Mouzon draws them
how_read: Re-traced 26 Nov 2026: snapped by program to the gap between Mouzon's double lines from end to end and checked by eye; ends joined to the road or town where Mouzon has them meet. Within about 1 km at the towns the fit holds (Camden, Orangeburg, Charles Town, Georgetown, Dorchester, Beaufort, Ninety Six, Long Bluff), about 3-5 km between them.

title: The Cherokee boundary (to 20 May 1777) and the lines with North Carolina (1735-72)
